arxiv-1909-11063.title: Trans-Planckian Censorship and the Swampland
arxiv-1909-11063.creator: Alek Bedroya and Cumrun Vafa
arxiv-1909-11063.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a new Swampland condition, the Trans-Planckian Censorship Conjecture (TCC), based on the idea that in a consistent quantum theory of gravity sub-Planckian quantum fluctuations should remain quantum and never become larger than the Hubble horizon and freeze in an expanding universe. TCC leads to conditions that are similar to the refined dS Swampland conjecture.

arxiv-2209-00728.title: Model Order Estimation in the Presence of multipath Interference using Residual Convolutional Neural Networks
arxiv-2209-00728.creator: Jianyuan Yu, William W. Howard, Yue Xu, R. Michael Buehrer
arxiv-2209-00728.description: Abstract Model order estimation (MOE) is often a pre-requisite for Direction of Arrival (DoA) estimation. Due to limits imposed by array geometry, it is typically not possible to estimate spatial parameters for an arbitrary number of sources; an estimate of the signal model is usually required. MOE is the process of selecting the most likely signal model from several candidates.

arxiv-2301-10737.title: Distributed Control of Partial Differential Equations Using Convolutional Reinforcement Learning Journal: Physica D
arxiv-2301-10737.creator: Sebastian Peitz, Jan Stenner, Vikas Chidananda, Oliver Wallscheid, Steven L. Brunton, Kunihiko Taira
arxiv-2301-10737.description: Abstract We present a convolutional framework which significantly reduces the complexity and thus, the computational effort for distributed reinforcement learning control of dynamical systems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). Exploiting translational equivariances, the high-dimensional distributed control problem can be transformed into a multi-agent control problem with many identical, uncoupled agents.

arxiv-2307-06875.title: Simultaneous calculation of elastic scattering, fusion, and direct cross sections for reactions of weakly-bound projectiles
arxiv-2307-06875.creator: H. M. Maridi, N. Keeley, K. Rusek
arxiv-2307-06875.description: Abstract Simultaneous analyses are performed of cross section data for elastic scattering, fusion, Coulomb breakup, and other direct yields for the 6 He+ 209 Bi system at near Coulomb-barrier energies. The bare and dynamical polarization potentials are constructed microscopically from the structure of the colliding nuclei and they reproduce all the data well with only two adjustable parameters.

arxiv-2401-01242.title: Encoding Binary Events from Continuous Time Series in Rooted Trees using Contrastive Learning
arxiv-2401-01242.creator: Tobias Engelhardt Rasmussen, Siv Sørensen
arxiv-2401-01242.description: Abstract Broadband infrastructure owners do not always know how their customers are connected in the local networks, which are structured as rooted trees. A recent study is able to infer the topology of a local network using discrete time series data from the leaves of the tree (customers).

arxiv-2404-05470.title: Towards Reconfigurable Linearizable Reads
arxiv-2404-05470.creator: Myles Thiessen, Aleksey Panas, Guy Khazma, Eyal de Lara
arxiv-2404-05470.description: Abstract . Linearizable datastores are desirable because they provide users with the illusion that the datastore is run on a single machine that performs client operations one at a time. To reduce the performance cost of providing this illusion, many specialized algorithms for linearizable reads have been proposed which significantly improve read performance compared to write performance.

arxiv-2506-06999.title: Towards Physics-informed Diffusion for Anomaly Detection in Trajectories
arxiv-2506-06999.creator: Arun Sharma, Mingzhou Yang, Majid Farhadloo, Subhankar Ghosh, Bharat Jayaprakash, Shashi Shekhar
arxiv-2506-06999.description: Abstract Given trajectory data, a domain-specific study area, and a user-defined threshold, we aim to find anomalous trajectories indicative of possible GPS spoofing (e.g., fake trajectory). The problem is societally important to curb illegal activities in international waters, such as unauthorized fishing and illicit oil transfers.

arxiv-2506-20872.title: Empowering Digital Agriculture: A Privacy-Preserving Framework for Data Sharing and Collaborative Research
arxiv-2506-20872.creator: Osama Zafar, Rosemarie Santa González, Mina Namazi, Alfonso Morales, Erman Ayday
arxiv-2506-20872.description: Abstract Data-driven agriculture, which integrates technology and data into agricultural practices, has the potential to improve crop yield, disease resilience, and long-term soil health. However, privacy concerns, such as adverse pricing, discrimination, and resource manipulation, deter farmers from sharing data, as it can be used against them.

arxiv-2510-11877.title: Robust Adversarial Reinforcement Learning in Stochastic Games via Sequence Modeling
arxiv-2510-11877.creator: Xiaohang Tang, Zhuowen Cheng, Satyabrat Kumar
arxiv-2510-11877.description: Abstract The Transformer, a highly expressive architecture for sequence modeling, has recently been adapted to solve sequential decision-making, most notably through the Decision Transformer (DT), which learns policies by conditioning on desired returns. Yet, the adversarial robustness of reinforcement learning methods based on sequence modeling remains largely unexplored.

europmc-pmc3237355.title: Seven-year neurodevelopmental scores and prenatal exposure to chlorpyrifos, a common agricultural pesticide.
europmc-pmc3237355.creator: Rauh V, Arunajadai S, Horton M, Perera F, Hoepner L, Barr DB, Whyatt R.
europmc-pmc3237355.description: Background In a longitudinal birth cohort study of inner-city mothers and children (Columbia Center for Children's Environmental Health), we have previously reported that prenatal exposure to chlorpyrifos (CPF) was associated with neurodevelopmental problems at 3 years of age. O

europmc-pmc9208265.title: Autophagy, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis in tumor immunotherapy.
europmc-pmc9208265.creator: Gao W, Wang X, Zhou Y, Wang X, Yu Y.
europmc-pmc9208265.description: In recent years, immunotherapy represented by immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) has led to unprecedented breakthroughs in cancer treatment. However, the fact that many tumors respond poorly or even not to ICIs, partly caused by the absence of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes...

pmc-10538455.title: Influence of sodium thiosulfate on coronary artery calcification of patients on dialysis: a meta-analysis
pmc-10538455.creator: Chong Huang, Zhibing Duan, Chengyun Xu, Yan Chen
pmc-10538455.description: Coronary artery calcification (CAC) is common in dialysis patients and is associated with a higher risk of future cardiovascular events. Sodium thiosulfate (STS) is effective for calciphylaxis in dialysis patients; however, the influence of STS on CAC in dialysis patients remains unclear.

pmc-10540342.title: A large-scale targeted proteomics of serum and tissue shows the utility of classifying high grade and low grade meningioma tumors
pmc-10540342.creator: Ankit Halder, Deeptarup Biswas, Aparna Chauhan, Adrita Saha, Shreeman Auromahima, Deeksha Yadav, Mehar Un Nissa, Gayatri Iyer, Shashwati Parihari, Gautam Sharma, Sridhar Epari, Prakash Shetty, Aliasgar Moiyadi, Graham Roy Ball, Sanjeeva Srivastava
pmc-10540342.description: BackgroundMeningiomas are the most prevalent primary brain tumors. Due to their increasing burden on healthcare, meningiomas have become a pivot of translational research globally. Despite many studies in the field of discovery proteomics, the identification of grade-specific markers for meningioma is still a paradox and requires thorough investigation.

pmc-11490576.title: LAP2α orchestrates alternative lengthening of telomeres suppression through telomeric heterochromatin regulation with HDAC1: unveiling a potential therapeutic target
pmc-11490576.creator: Bing Wang, Haomeng Kou, Yuwen Wang, Qi Zhang, Duo Jiang, Juan Wang, Ziqin Zhao, Yao Zhou, Miaomiao Zhang, Lei Sui, Mingfeng Zhao, Yancheng Liu, Yang Liu, Lei Shi, Feng Wang
pmc-11490576.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In response to the challenge of telomere attrition during DNA replication, cancer cells predominantly employ telomerase or, in 10–15% of cases, the alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT). The intricate details of ALT, however, remain elusive. In this study, we unveil that the knockdown of lamina-associated polypeptide 2 alpha (LAP2α) in ALT cells results in telomere dysfunction, triggering a notable increase in ALT-associated hallmarks, including high frequencies of PML bodies (APBs), C-rich extrachromosomal circles (C-circles), and telomere sister chromatid exchange (T-SCE).

pmc-11504981.title: Do Chinese Preschool Children Love Their Motherland? Evidence from the Game-Based Assessment
pmc-11504981.creator: Qianqian Liu, Xiumin Hong, Pier Luigi Sacco
pmc-11504981.description: Patriotism is a topic of significant importance in many countries around the world. Preschool children play a crucial role in shaping the future, and their patriotism is closely linked to the future development of their nation. Currently, the game-based assessment has advantages over traditional evaluation methods and is more suitable for preschool children.

pmc-11520600.title: The relationship between childhood SES and health in middle and old age: evidence from China
pmc-11520600.creator: Chen Yu-cheng, Gao Gong-jing
pmc-11520600.description: ObjectiveDrawing from the extended Grossman health capital and demand theory and the life course theory, this study examined whether childhood SES has direct and significant correlation with health in middle and old age in a specific historical context in China.MethodsA sample of 9,861 respondents was obtained from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS).

pmc-11536005.title: The bio-artificial pancreas to treat type 1 diabetes: Perspectives from healthcare professionals in the Netherlands
pmc-11536005.creator: Dide de Jongh, Eline Bunnik, Behiye Ozcan, Robert Zietse, Emma Massey, VANGUARD consortium
pmc-11536005.description: Highlights•Recipients will have more mental space to focus on other aspects in life.•The invisibility of the BAP could enhance the sense of ‘normality’ for recipients.•Implementing the BAP could lower public healthcare costs.•There are concerns about safety, inequitable access and relinquishing control.

pmc-11714252.title: Prediction of long‐term treatment outcome in Alzheimer's disease based on EEG connectivity
pmc-11714252.creator: Tak Youn, Hea Jeong Park, Hyong Sook Jun
pmc-11714252.description: BackgroundIt is difficult to predict of long‐term treatment response of AD to medical treatment when starting medication. We explored EEG brain connectivity as a potential biomarker for long‐term medication outcomes in patients with AD.MethodsResting‐state EEG was recorded from a total of 56 AD patients (mean age = 73.23±6.39) when starting medication after diagnosis of AD.

pmc-11895607.title: HLA‐DR genotypes in patients with primary Sjögren's syndrome in Taiwan
pmc-11895607.creator: Chang‐Yi Yen, Pin‐Yi Wang, Kuan‐Yu Chen, Chia‐Chun Tseng, Cheng‐Chin Wu, Tsan‐Teng Ou, Jeng‐Hsien Yen
pmc-11895607.description: Different human leukocyte antigen (HLA) genotypes have been known to be associated with the risk of development of Sjögren's syndrome in different populations, but this association has never been reported in Taiwan. We enrolled 1044 subjects (673 patients, 371 controls) and tested their HLA‐DR genotypes. We found an increased risk of Sjögren's syndrome in patients carrying HLA‐DR8.

pmc-12547150.title: RoseLeafSet: Real-world leaf image dataset for AI-based agricultural solutions
pmc-12547150.creator: Jarin Tasmim Jinia, Md Sakibur Rahman, Mayen Uddin Mojumdar, Md Hasan Imam Bijoy
pmc-12547150.description: This study highlights the growing significance of flowers, especially roses, in the global agricultural market, where they are cultivated for both personal enjoyment and commercial purposes. Among these, roses are considered one of the most popular and widely cultivated flowers.

pmc-12587424.title: Adjustments of plant primary metabolism in the face of climate change
pmc-12587424.creator: Mustafa Bulut, Esra Karakas, Alisdair R Fernie
pmc-12587424.description: Plant metabolism is profoundly affected by various abiotic stresses. Consequently, plants must reconfigure their metabolic networks to sustain homeostasis while synthesizing compounds that mitigate stress. This aspect, with the current intensified climate impact results in more frequent abiotic stresses on a global scale.

pmc-12653132.title: Surgical Outcomes and Complications of Distal Nasal Reconstruction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-12653132.creator: Giovanni Salzano, Veronica Scocca, Antonio Romano, Luigi Angelo Vaira, Jerome R. Lechien, Fabio Maglitto, Marzia Petrocelli, Giovanni Dell’Aversana Orabona
pmc-12653132.description: Background: Reconstruction of the distal nose represents a major surgical challenge due to the aesthetic and functional relevance of this subunit. Various techniques—including local, regional and free flaps and grafts—have been described, but high-quality evidence comparing outcomes remains limited. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Embase, and Google Scholar.

pmc-12755388.title: Incidencia de dengue y su relación con el índice oceánico de El Niño, como variable sensible para anticipar brotes en la región Caribe colombiana
pmc-12755388.creator: Alexander Salazar-Ceballos, Lídice Álvarez-Miño
pmc-12755388.description: ResumenIntroducción. El informe Lancet Countdown 2023 para Latinoamérica indica que el aumento de las temperaturas influye en la transmisión del virus del dengue. En la región Caribe de Colombia, se ha identificado una asociación significativa entre la incidencia de dengue y variables climáticas, como la temperatura, la humedad y la precipitación.Objetivo.

pmc-13176803.title: SCORTEN and Novel Prognostic Markers in Stevens–Johnson Syndrome/Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-13176803.creator: Zhao Feng Liu, Howard Yang, Lawrence Lin, Ash Tyagi, Amy Sylivris, Adithya Shastry, Nidhin Sunil Kuruvilla, Douglas Gin, Christopher Y. Chew
pmc-13176803.description: Stevens–Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS/TEN) is a rare, severe skin reaction with high mortality, most often triggered by medications. Early identification of patients at risk is essential for guiding treatment. The SCORTEN score, comprising seven clinical and laboratory variables, is widely used to predict mortality but may have limitations across different populations.

pmc-13326145.title: The impact of war on Primary Health Care in Ukraine: a cross-sectional survey and qualitative interviews with service providers
pmc-13326145.creator: Adrianna Murphy, Kaija Kasekamp, Olga Demeshko, Jarno Habicht
pmc-13326145.description: BackgroundPrimary Health Care (PHC) is vital to supporting emergency preparedness and health care resilience. There is limited evidence of the impact of crises on PHC services and financing. We aimed to explore the impact of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 on PHC services in the country.MethodsWe used a mixed-methods approach.
